name: Revolutionary nationalism
summary: Revolutionary nationalism is a label for nationalist movements that pursue independence or national renewal by overthrowing the existing order, typically through armed struggle against colonial or foreign domination. In its mainstream anti-colonial form it ties political independence to economic transformation, mass participation and a people's right to its own history and culture, usually with a socialist or anti-imperialist orientation.
scope: The anti-colonial national-liberation strand of the 20th century, based on Amilcar Cabral and the PAIGC and Frantz Fanon, with examples from Sandino, the Irish revolutionaries and Eritrea in the Wikipedia overview. Excludes fascist-style national rebirth movements and purely electoral nationalism; because the label is descriptive rather than a single doctrine, many answers are low-confidence inferences.

sources.usedFor: PAIGC practice: bazaars, medical teams, education, women on councils, People's Assembly.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred: Cabral's PAIGC ran medical teams for fighters and civilians in liberated zones, suggesting state-provided care, but no healthcare program is stated.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Adherents mostly led agrarian anti-colonial struggles and the label gives no wage-policy doctrine; strands split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Inferred from the stress on breaking imperialist capitalist structures and Fanon's distrust of the market-linked national bourgeoisie.

public-ownership.rationale: Cabral says liberation must destroy the imposed capitalist structure and points toward socialism; Fanon warns nationalization can merely hand privilege to local elites, so support is conditioned.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from hostility to the compradore bourgeoisie and the push to redirect surplus to the people; no tax programme is cited.

unions-good.rationale: Sources mention worker resistance to foreign ownership (Mexican railway workers) but the movements usually put the nation ahead of any sectional organisation.

property-fundamental.rationale: Fanon argues the land belongs to those who till it and that elites' privileges must be overturned, so property rights are subordinate to national and popular claims.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Opposition to foreign economic control implies tight regulation of foreign firms; domestic corporate regulation is not specifically addressed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the people-centred, service-providing practice of the PAIGC in liberated areas.

worker-ownership.rationale: Cabral looks to socialism but stresses each country's own reality rather than a model of worker ownership; adherents are split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Never addressed directly; Fanon criticizes party informant networks but revolutionary movements also rely on security measures.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; no basis for a firm inference.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Fanon warns nationalism decays into chauvinism and racism, but no stance on legal restriction is given.

strong-leader.rationale: Movements were often built around charismatic leaders, yet Fanon attacks the leader who pacifies the people; adherents are split.

state-harmful.rationale: These movements aim to seize and build a sovereign national state; Cabral expects a state to inherit power and Fanon wants it democratized, not abolished.

limit-guns.rationale: Armed struggle is central, but a post-liberation gun policy is not specified; split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Fanon warns the army and police become pillars of an elite regime, while liberation armies are central heroes; split.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed by the documented sources.

traditional-family.rationale: Cabral demanded women's full participation, yet many strands uphold tradition; split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred: historical revolutionary nationalist movements generally did not champion it; contested and anachronistic.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between socially conservative and progressive strands.

more-religion-public.rationale: Eritrean PFDJ stresses religious pluralism but other strands are religiously inflected; split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial redress of colonial domination and, in the US case, black nationalist strands.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No stated position; Cabral stressed women's participation but not gender theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cabral grounds liberation in a people's own history and culture, and Fanon devotes his analysis to national culture in the fight for freedom.

gradual-change.rationale: Cabral holds compromise with imperialism fails and armed revolution is the normal path, rejecting gradualism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not a defining issue; movements aimed at colonial settlers rather than immigration policy.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from insistence on national sovereignty and distrust of imperialist institutions; solidarity is among peoples, not through global bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Cabral describes imperialism as piracy and a stage of capitalism, and Fanon sees open exports of raw materials as perpetuating dependency.

nation-first.rationale: Putting the nation's liberation and development first is central, though Cabral also stresses solidarity among struggling peoples.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism: foreign intervention is mostly seen as imperialist pretext.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from the focus on bounded national units; pan-African unity is a separate aim.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred from the stress on development to overcome colonial underdevelopment.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Cabral was an agronomist valuing practical knowledge, but nothing states a general techno-optimism.

revolution-justified.rationale: Revolution against the existing order is the defining feature of the label, and Cabral calls armed struggle the normal path of national liberation.

experts-over-public.rationale: Fanon prescribes direct popular participation and political education over elite direction.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred from Cabral's socialist path; adherents differ and he stresses suiting local economic conditions.

socialized-markets.rationale: Cabral allows a freed nation to adopt the structure that suits it; not specified.

land-value-tax.rationale: The tradition gives no fiscal doctrine on land taxation, so adherents are not placed either way.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; inferred sympathy for redistribution is too weak to score.

basic-income.rationale: No documented position; the movements were concerned with land, independence and mass mobilisation rather than income schemes.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Opposition to foreign economic control and Fanon's concern with dependence support protecting domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: National economic sovereignty after liberation implies state steering; Fanon warns against foreign-owned assembly plants.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Fanon favors land to the tiller and cooperatives, but others favor state ownership; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Socialism is the goal but abolition of money is not part of the national-liberation programme.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: sovereign states controlling their own finances is the aim, not market money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; some regimes were corporatist but others not.

one-party-rule.rationale: Many liberation movements ruled through a single party, yet Fanon calls it a dictatorship of the bourgeoisie; the tradition is divided.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Revolutionary overthrow of the existing order generally targets monarchies and colonial rulers.

democracy-best.rationale: Fanon wants popular participation but rejects elite parliamentarism; split and contested.

direct-votes.rationale: Fanon argues people should take part in decisions directly, but the tradition is not committed to referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: national party or front structures dominate, though Fanon prefers decentralized popular bodies.

right-to-secede.rationale: Nationalists claim secession from empire for their own nation but typically oppose further splitting after independence; split.

natural-rulers.rationale: Denies colonial and class claims to rule; the people regain their own history and power.

political-violence-never.rationale: Armed struggle is central and Cabral deems it the normal route to liberation.

war-builds-character.rationale: Fanon treats violence as liberating, but Cabral framed war as necessity not virtue; split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Eritrean PFDJ stresses pluralism; Irish and others integrated religion; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred from national-unity framing that avoids a single religious law, but not stated.

private-courts-defense.rationale: National sovereignty and state power over defence are fundamental.

military-superiority.rationale: Movements were weak and focused on liberation; no stated aim of superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Cabral built unity across diverse communities and Fanon warns that tribalism and racism corrode national consciousness.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Cabral's own theory held class and people-level factors (the economic base and its history) shape struggle, but he emphasised national liberation as the key struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed; inferred sympathy for equality too vague.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Sandino-style struggles defended native lands from foreign occupation; indigenous peoples as a category not directly addressed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from imperialism as piracy and usurpation of a people's history; reparations are not cited.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-African unity appears for Cabral, but religion-based unions are not; split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Fanon criticises elites pursuing self-interest, and movements emphasise collective sacrifice (class suicide).

duties-before-rights.rationale: Cabral demanded sacrifice (class suicide), yet movements also claim rights; split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics lies outside the anti-colonial sources consulted, so there is no basis for a position.

limit-population.rationale: The sources do not address population policy; Cabral blames imperialist structures rather than numbers for poverty.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred: development is wanted, though colonial extraction is condemned.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No stated view on speeding technological change; the sources focus on liberation and political control.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on popular political education and participation.

restore-past-order.rationale: The ideology seeks revolution against existing order, not restoration; though some strands invoke pre-colonial heritage.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Cabral stressed pragmatic local reality yet insisted on theory; split.

direct-action.rationale: Armed struggle and mass mobilisation over compromise are central, though movements also built parties and assemblies.

means-match-ends.rationale: Fanon argues methods shape outcomes but others justify violence by liberation; split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Development and independent modern nationhood are the aim.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not a national liberation aim; inferred from practical state building.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Socialist orientation suggests sympathy but is not stated as an ultimate aim.

production-for-use.rationale: Cabral's socialist path implies production for the people's needs, inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Cabral calls imperialism piracy and capital's last phase; domestic profit as exploitation is inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Cabral explicitly stressed that revolutions cannot be copied and that the peasantry and petty bourgeoisie, not a proletariat, were the agents.

collective-farming.rationale: Fanon prefers cooperatives under democratic control but also land to the tiller; split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Cabral calls imperialism the last phase of capitalism; war claim inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: State-building movements treat taxes as legitimate national revenue.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal theories of state limits are not addressed by the sources, and revolutionary movements justify restrictions by the national cause.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights of peoples, such as to their own history, are central.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from mass mobilisation in liberation armies.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from commitment to national belonging and the struggle.

state-as-business.rationale: Fanon and Cabral treat the state as an instrument of popular liberation.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from Fanon's concern for material and social conditions behind formal independence.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources say nothing of universities and media holding power; the question belongs to other debates.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Fanon explicitly traces racism as a corruption of nationalism, and anticolonial movements rejected racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporate representation by families and trade bodies is not part of the documented national-liberation programme.

total-state.rationale: Fanon warns against the elite party state suppressing criticism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Revolutionary nationalism aims at renewal of a people regaining its own history, though the decadence framing is fascist-inflected.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Movements are anti-imperialist and defensive; expansion is the opposite of their anti-imperial identity.

bound-labor.rationale: Fanon argues land belongs to those who till it, opposing bound labor.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Cabral treats history as usurped by imperialism and culture as political; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Cabral grounds rights in peoples' own histories while appealing to universal solidarity; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Unity of the nation is stressed but Fanon wants popular conflict over class; split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Contested within the anti-colonial family; revolutionary nationalism has examples on both sides.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; some nationalisms assert it and others do not, so no position can be shown.

revive-national-language.rationale: Cultural revival features in national movements such as the Irish; inferred and not universal.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Fanon wants democratic control of cooperatives; otherwise unspecified.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from PAIGC priority on public education in liberated zones.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Macroeconomic deficit policy is not addressed by the sources consulted.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred: political independence is held to require economic transformation, not liberalism.

rule-by-example.rationale: Cabral's class suicide asks leaders to model sacrifice, but laws also matter; split.

national-self-determination.rationale: Cabral grounds liberation in the inalienable right of every people to its own history, and it is the core demand.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred split: armed liberation claims its own legitimacy, but a state's foreign force is not addressed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The sources do not take a side between reason and faith; the movements included both secular and religious adherents.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The tradition is silent on welfare eligibility for immigrants; its concerns were colonial rule and independence.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare conditions are not discussed in the national-liberation sources.

class-collaboration.rationale: Cabral's petty bourgeoisie must commit class suicide and the ties to imperialist capital are rejected, though national fronts unite classes against the colonizer.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Culture and history are the ground of resistance, so heritage is not sacrificed.

dominated-front.rationale: Cabral's Tricontinental address calls for active solidarity among Africa, Asia and Latin America against imperialism.

workers-nation.rationale: Revolutionary nationalism organizes people nationally against foreign domination rather than via an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Cabral said the revolution cannot win without women's full participation, and the PAIGC mandated women on councils.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury bans appear in some religious movements but not in the documented core of the ideology.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Anti-colonial movements opposed racial classification; Fanon denounces racism as a decay of nationalism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Fanon sees the post-colonial state as serving the elite, but not as a general theory; inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production policy is not addressed; foreign control of resources is the likelier concern.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: French revolutionary nationalism assimilated by cultural adoption, while other strands pluralist; split.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy of replacement is not part of the tradition.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the sources, so adherents are not placed.

national-mission.rationale: Cabral denies that revolutions can be exported or copied, though French revolutionary nationalism did claim a mission; the mainstream here rejects it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Cabral's insistence on women's participation suggests recognition of structural exclusion; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Fanon denounces the national bourgeoisie and leader who protect elite interests.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contradicts the humanist anti-racism of these movements.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred: colonial repression is condemned; accountability for one's own forces is uncertain.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Movements seek a strong sovereign state reshaping the economic structure.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Fanon rejects racism as national decay.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Anti-colonial movements claim equal worth and rights against colonial hierarchy.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Cabral said each country must follow its own reality, and national liberation can proceed one nation at a time.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Opposition to settler domination such as the US occupation of Nicaragua and colonial rule implies this view, but cases vary.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; plural Eritrean model stresses pluralism.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from pluralist national unity stance.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle protection belongs to Hindu nationalist debate and is not part of the anti-colonial sources here.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The sources give no position on religious teaching; the Eritrean example stresses pluralism but not school policy.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Cabral built village councils and a People's Assembly to rest authority on the people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export targets are not addressed; sources object to dependency but do not set trade-balance aims.

population-transfer.rationale: Fanon denounces ethnic chauvinism and racism; unity across diverse communities was the aim.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Cabral deems armed struggle justified, and movements initiate force against the existing order.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Inferred from solidarity and unity against imperialism.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Freedom from imperialist domination is central, but republican theory is not invoked.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; Fanon wants decentralised participation.

vanguard-party.rationale: Cabral calls for a firmly united vanguard, though his vanguard was a national party rather than a proletarian one.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Fanon and Cabral make the peasants and the masses the centre of the revolution.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing sales are a British policy debate not covered by the sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is not discussed; movements prized national unity but sources give no rule.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Cabral locates poverty in imperialist structures, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cabral built unity among diverse communities.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is never mentioned in the consulted sources.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Fanon criticizes repression, yet movements run emergency regimes; split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The PAIGC bazaars sold goods below colonial prices, an example of intervening in essential supplies.

party-controls-media.rationale: Fanon criticises party informant systems, but some regimes controlled media; split.

party-commands-army.rationale: Liberation movements often put the army under the party; not stated.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Cabral asks for a united vanguard; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation timing is outside the documented concerns of the anti-colonial movements.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Cabral's class suicide implies leaders sharing the people's condition; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sovereignty gained by liberation is not readily pooled, though pan-African union appears.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Constitutional allocation of command is not addressed by the sources.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not part of the political programme described by the sources.

clerical-rule.rationale: Revolutionary nationalism is a secular-political project; clerical rule not part.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist loyalty vs class split.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The sources do not address censorship of art; Fanon sees national culture as a living part of the fight, not an object of moral policing.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; some leaders did stay.

recall-officials.rationale: Fanon wants leaders accountable to a mobilised people; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Independence from imperialist blocs is central, though solidarity with other peoples is welcomed.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure rules are not addressed by the sources.

people-in-arms.rationale: Armed peasants and guerrillas are central to national liberation war.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Fanon and Cabral centred peasants but not as a moral claim; split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National unity is a central aim, such as in Eritrea or Ireland.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Cabral expects the petty bourgeoisie to lead while demanding class suicide; split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cabral grounds each people's right to its own culture and history without hierarchy.

death-penalty.rationale: The sources do not state a view on capital punishment; revolutionary movements varied in practice.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School curriculum on sexuality is not addressed by the sources.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on modern education.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and strands differ between conservative and progressive social outlooks.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Cabral's inclusive unity across communities points away from descent-based membership; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; unity versus pluralism split.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The sources do not address exemptions from general law for religious minorities.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on unity and sacrifice.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist critique of economic dependence.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Cabral says neo-colonial independence must destroy the imposed capitalist structure, and Fanon argues independence leaves the economy unchanged.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Cabral began a People's Assembly to prepare independence; constitutional procedure is not stated.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Fanon criticises elite authoritarianism but regimes justified it; split.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aid is distrusted as dependency but exploitation is condemned; split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear forces are anachronistic for the movements studied, which fought guerrilla wars.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources give no position on how heads of state should be chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Sovereign economic control is the aim.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Land to the tiller and national need over elite privilege.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; movements often allied with the USSR.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation doctrine is anachronistic and absent from the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Mutual-defence pacts are not discussed; solidarity among struggling peoples is stated but not as a treaty obligation.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Opposition to foreign occupation, as in the Nicaragua case, implies this stance.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state relations are not addressed in the sources consulted.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources are silent on a ceremonial or non-party head of state.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special autonomy within a larger state is not discussed; the movements sought their own nation-state.

character-from-environment.rationale: Class suicide and Cabral's materialist emphasis on conditions suggest this; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is anachronistic for these movements and absent from the sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-government theory is not part of the documented ideology.

leader-cult.rationale: Fanon criticises the leader who pacifies the people, yet cults of leaders arose; split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are not addressed by the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Cabral wrote about the colonial and neocolonial phase, not about class struggle after socialism is built.

land-redistribution.rationale: Fanon argues the land belongs to those who till it and argues for redistribution.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from national right to homeland.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Cabral rejected ethnic framing and borders are largely accepted; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Cabral insisted on women's full participation.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not addressed; only pan-African unity in general appears in the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-African unity appears in Cabral's activity (MPLA, solidarity).

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The aim is a state of the nation itself, not autonomy within another state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Cabral held that economic base and history decide revolution and that the petty bourgeoisie lacks the economic base for power.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition law is not addressed; the sources concentrate on foreign domination of the economy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Constraints on courts are not covered by the sources, so adherents are left undetermined.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The PAIGC required women hold at least two of five seats on village councils.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Fanon wants less dependence but not autarky; split.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-agreement standards are not addressed by the sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: Class suicide and sacrifice suggest moral commitment; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Cabral's war was built on mass politicisation, while foco claims are Guevarist; split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Overthrowing the old order generally targets hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Cabral's right of a people to its own history supports teaching nation-centred history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Cabral rejects imperialism as piracy and usurpation of history.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from redress of historical injustice.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary system design is not discussed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Cabral views imperialism as capitalism's last phase.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The tradition resists former colonisers' influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Cabral said a nation adopts the structure best suiting it; split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Cabral and Fanon do not take up the Leninist labor-aristocracy thesis in the passages consulted.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Entrenched constitutional rights are not addressed in the sources.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from rejection of colonial usurpation; though borders mostly stayed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Cabral's village councils and People's Assembly suggest popular selection; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Collective unity and revolutionary discipline are stressed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resisting unjust rulers is the ideology's foundation, applied to colonial rulers and later elites.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics lies outside the sources consulted.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed by the sources consulted.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Fanon wants mass participation, not paternalism.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Active commitment and sacrifice are demanded.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Fanon says the leader pacifies the people but media not addressed.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed; Cabral stresses culture but not hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Cabral describes imperialism as piracy and failing the role capital played at home; Fanon says export economy remains.

native-born-offices.rationale: Eligibility for public office is not addressed in the sources; Cabral's inclusive unity does not settle it.

party-own-road.rationale: Cabral insists revolutions cannot be copied and must fit each country's reality.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Fanon warns of dependence through foreign capital.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist demands are not part of the core documented positions; cases differ.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Colonial settler domination is rejected; stated for Africa but not general.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional anti-fascism is a European debate not found in the sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anti-imperialists generally reject cold-war equivalence framing; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: This historical dispute about the US Civil War is not part of the ideology.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The sources do not address commemoration of contested figures.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Cabral's gender focus was women's participation in the revolution.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not addressed in the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Cabral held that each country's own economic, social, cultural reality must shape its path.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Fanon warns of army pillars of elite rule; liberation armies are central; split.

paid-care-work.rationale: Unpaid care work is not discussed by the sources consulted.

filial-duty.rationale: Family obligations are not addressed in the sources, and adherents are split between traditionalist and modernising strands.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service recruitment is not discussed in the sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Opposition to foreign economic control supports blocking takeovers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not addressed by the sources.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Fanon wants leaders bound to the mobilised people; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land to the tiller echoes it but not community ownership; split.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not addressed; Cabral's People's Assembly was only a preparatory body.

decide-locally.rationale: Movements stress a unified national front; Fanon wants decentralised party structures, but sovereignty rests with the nation.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Fanon is sceptical of elite parliamentarism while Cabral built a People's Assembly; no settled view on parliamentary supremacy.

missingStatements.text: The petty bourgeoisie that leads independence must give up its class interests and identify with the working masses.
missingStatements.rationale: Cabral's class suicide thesis is a defining claim about who leads national liberation.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Cabral's theory of class suicide; too narrow for other ideologies to take a side on.

missingStatements.text: Political independence from a colonial power should be won by armed struggle rather than negotiation.
missingStatements.rationale: Cabral calls armed struggle the normal way of national liberation imposed by imperialist repression.

notes: The label is descriptive and covers movements from left anti-colonial to authoritarian military regimes; this profile follows the left anti-colonial mainstream, and the Cabral and Fanon sources partly disagree on one-party rule.
